title: Limits and Continuity in Higher Dimensions
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar

definitions.title: Limit of a Function of Two Variables
definitions.statement: For every epsilon > 0 there exists a delta > 0 such that |f(x, y) - L| < epsilon whenever (x, y) is in the domain of f and 0 < sqrt((x - x_0)^2 + (y - y_0)^2) < delta.
conditions: (x_0, y_0) is an accumulation point of the domain
Delta applies across all approach paths
definitions.explanation: In two dimensions, approach paths are uncountably infinite (lines, parabolas, spirals). The limit exists if and only if every possible path yields the identical limit L.
definitions.keyTakeaway: If two different paths to (x_0, y_0) yield different limits, the limit does not exist (Two-Path Test).

definitions.title: Continuity of Multivariable Functions
definitions.statement: A function f(x, y) is continuous at an interior point (x_0, y_0) if f is defined at (x_0, y_0), the limit exists as (x, y) -> (x_0, y_0), and the limit equals the function value.
definitions.explanation: Polynomials, rational functions, and compositions of continuous single-variable functions with continuous multivariable functions are continuous on their natural domains.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Allows direct substitution evaluation at points of continuity.
